skill_entry.name: 14. New code re-derives what an existing helper already provides
skill_entry.trigger: Any one of these in the diff's added production lines (h/ and src/, never t/; greps in procedures.md): (a) a `getenv("NAME")` (environment-variable read) or other configuration read whose topic (HW_ATTN) an existing function already reads or decides, under any variable name; (b) a busy-wait loop on a memory word where the project has a wait primitive (mwaitx); (c) a numeric literal passed to a configure, init or setup call whose parameter is a model- or hardware-derived quantity (scalar, head_size); (d) a per-model formula (`1.0f / sqrtf(head_size)`) a constructor or config object already computes with more branches; (e) a one-formula helper the diff adds while the same operands stand inline elsewhere; (f) an added if/else whose bodies differ ONLY by a type name or one string literal, shown by a line diff; (g) a commit/guard/push sequence copied whole to a second site under an ordering comment; (h) a call right after a loop whose callee walks the same container; (i) a grow loop beside a `resize` on a sibling member.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Collect candidates with the kind (a)-(i) greps over `git diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src`. Drop a line whose paired removed line carries the same call or formula (a re-spelling, tron-3756). 2. Find the owner outside the hunk at HEAD and at BASE: topic stem for (a) (TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN -> HW_ATTN), the wait primitive name for (b), the parameter stem for (c)(d), the formula operands for (e), each call name for (g); list the owner's callers. 3. Only when BASE has no owner, search the base branch with `--not HEAD` and `--until` the review date. 4. Read both sides; write every difference: operand type, alignment, element state, extra branches, the differing tokens of twin branches, a conjunct the helper does not cover. 5. For (g) confirm the hunk added the whole sequence, count the copies at HEAD, find the originating commit. 6. For (a) across the layering rule propose an `extern` declaration. 7. Report with per-kind counters.
skill_entry.question: Does a function or expression that already exists at HEAD, or on the PR's base branch before the review date, compute this value, decide this predicate, perform this wait or carry this ordered sequence, and can the author name a difference in what that helper accepts or produces that the output depends on?
skill_entry.do_not_fire:
- The helper cannot accept the input: operand type or alignment (1920, loop kept at the approved head), or element state the stdlib call does not produce (2461, Wade withdrew). A second configuration knob (another variable name, default or read-once) is NOT a difference: that knob is what the helper replaces (2287).
- A value a local or sibling member in the same scope already holds (`nshards` beside `shards.size()`): the redundant-code check (3029340601, 3010846319, 2913598312).
- A bare literal with no owning value in h/ or src/: check 13.
- Duplicates inside t/.
- A long pre-existing function grown further (3405172585: later step).
- Re-spelling, rename, formatting (tron-3756, tron-3741).
- A hot-path cost argument alone.
- Near-twin branches differing by an intrinsic, an argument or a return (tron-2693, 1707, 2646).
- An inline copy kept for another consumer at the approved head (441e81178b self_attention.hpp:797, :837, :1499).
skill_entry.finding_shape: "`<new expression or loop>` (<file:line>) re-derives <quantity> that `<helper>` (<file:line>) already <computes | reads | waits for>; `<site A>` (line <a>) and `<site B>` (line <b>) call the helper. Suggest one helper for all <N>, so the copies can't drift if the convention changes." Question form when the helper is a project primitive: "couldn't we use `<helper>` for this (and the <sibling site>)?" Statement form when the value has one owner: "the <quantity> needs to come from the model... `<literal>` is not the correct value, currently". For a conjunction name only the conjunct to replace (2287 kept `have_devices &&`). For a copied sequence: a numbered list of the copies and the consequence sentence, no block.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: "Nit:" for a key computed two ways (4147010638). No severity word, a plain question, for a primitive the project already has ("couldn't we use mwaitx::wait_for_not_event for this", 2719158416; "you should be able to use `resize` for this...?", 3102140611). Plain statement when he owns or knows the helper ("this should be replaced with the `fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` function I just added early this week", 3029194687) or when the literal is wrong for the model ("1.0f is not the correct value, currently", 2897190682). For a copied safety-critical sequence: a numbered list of the copies and the consequence sentence ("a missed copy would be a silent staging-lifetime bug rather than a compile error", 3907214892), still no block and no CHANGES_REQUESTED. His softest form is a question with an admitted constraint: "could we maybe ... just looking for an alternative" (3454460758); he does not use the word minor there.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at the reviewed commit (three line numbers across one file, 4147010638); other files in h/ and src/ at HEAD and at BASE (the helper's definition, the model state constructor, the layering rule in README.code-org.md); callers of the helper; the PR's base branch log before the review date, excluding the PR's own commits; the commit that introduced an ordered sequence (git log -S; Wade's own attribution '#3928' in 3907214892 is his, the log gives PR 2906 and 3385). Not the PR body, not CI, not runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: new code re-derives what an existing helper already provides

Common setup as above (HEAD, WT, N), with two changes for this check. BASE is the merge-base with the PR's own base branch, not origin/main: `BASE_REF=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$BASE_REF)`. For a merged PR, BASE is the parent of the PR's first commit (`git -C WT rev-parse <first commit>^`). Record `git -C WT rev-list --count --no-merges BASE..HEAD`; more than about 100 commits means the base branch is wrong (PR 2287: base hwattention_sync gives ba1bed266d and 5 commits; origin/main gives 77195bba8c and 462 commits).

1. Candidates, production code only:
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src > prod.diff
# (a) configuration reads
grep -n -E '^\+.*(std::)?getenv\("[A-Z0-9_]+"' prod.diff
# (b) busy-wait loops on a memory word
grep -n -E '^\+.*while \(\*?[A-Za-z_>.-]+ *!= *[A-Za-z_]+\)' prod.diff; grep -n -E '^\+.*(rdtsc\(\)|ns_to_cycles|timeout_cycles)' prod.diff
# (c) literal arguments inside a configure/init/setup call (comment lines dropped)
grep -n -E '^\+[^/]*(configure|_init|setup)[A-Za-z_]*\([^)]*\b[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+f?)?\b' prod.diff | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+ *//'
# (d) per-model formulas written out (sqrt or a division next to the operand; a bare head_size argument is not a formula)
grep -n -E '^\+.*((1(\.0f?)?|1\.f) */ *(std::)?sqrtf?\(|rsqrt\(|/ *(std::)?sqrtf?\([^)]*head_size)' prod.diff
# (e) one-formula helpers the diff adds
grep -n -E '^\+ *return [A-Za-z_.()]+ *[-+*/] *[A-Za-z_.()]+( *[-+*/] *[A-Za-z_.()]+)?;' prod.diff
# (f) if/else candidates: list added `} else {` lines
grep -n -E '^\+ *\} else \{' prod.diff
# (g) ordered sequences
grep -n -E '^\+.*\.(commit|push|push_back)\(' prod.diff
# (h) loops over a sized container, (i) resize calls
grep -n -E '^\+.*(while|for) \(.*\.size\(\)' prod.diff; grep -n -E '^\+.*\.resize\(' prod.diff
```
   Filters applied to the collected lines before step 2:
   - Drop a line whose paired removed line (the `-` line of the same hunk) carries the same call name, member name or formula: a re-spelled argument, a rename or a reformat adds no copy (tron-3756 src/tron/gof.cpp:272 re-spells `tracker.push(static_cast<uint32_t>(sh->dev->idx),` as `tracker.push(` with the typed id).
   - (c): open the callee's declaration; keep the hit only when the parameter name stem is a model or hardware quantity (scalar, scale, head_size, n_heads, n_layers).
   - (f): map the hit to its HEAD line through the `@@` header, print 40 lines around it (`git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n 'L-20,L+20p'`), find the matching `if (` and the closing brace by indentation, record A1,A2 (if body) and B1,B2 (else body). Skip a hit whose else body is one log or return statement.
   - (g): keep a hit only when the same two or three call names appear in the same order within five added lines at a second site, and either site, or the function at BASE the sequence came from, carries a comment with 'order', 'before', 'after', 'must', 'live' or 'disarm'. Record dropped sites as 'no ordering comment'.
   - (h): keep only when the first call after the loop's closing brace names a function whose body walks the same container (open it). (i): keep only a `while (x.size() < n) x.push_back(...)` or `for` grow loop within five lines of a `.resize(` on a sibling member.
   Record the count per kind and the count dropped per reason.
2. For each surviving candidate, the owner outside the hunk, at HEAD and at BASE:
```
git -C WT grep -n '<operand>' HEAD -- h src | grep -v '<candidate file>:<candidate line>'
git -C WT grep -n '<operand>' BASE -- h src
git -C WT grep -n '<helper>' HEAD -- h src      # the owner's callers
```
   Operand per kind. (a): the topic stem of the variable name, with the prefix (TRON_, POS_, RZ_) and the verb word (USE_, ENABLE_, DISABLE_, NO_) stripped; run `git -C WT grep -n -E 'getenv\("[A-Z0-9_]*<STEM>[A-Z0-9_]*"' HEAD -- h src` (every environment read on the topic) and `git -C WT grep -n -i -E '<stem>_(enabled|disabled|on|off)\(' HEAD -- h src` (the predicate helpers). On 2287 (HEAD 4274d5878a) stem HW_ATTN yields USE_HW_ATTN at hw_attn_config.hpp:19 inside `fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` (:17) with callers stream_generate.hpp:429, model.hpp:1434, self_attention.hpp:387, :699, :945; the raw variable name TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN finds only the hunk. (b): `wait_for_not_event\|wait_for_event\|wait_for_geq` (h/pos/mwaitx.hpp at early-2026 heads). (c),(d): the parameter stem (`pre_attn_scalar`, `hw_attn_cfg`). (e): the helper's formula operands (`num_workers() - n_attn_workers`). (g): each call name.
3. Only when step 2 found no owner at BASE, search the base branch:
```
git -C WT log --format='%h %ad %an %s' --date=short --until=<review date or today> -S'<operand>' BASE..origin/$BASE_REF --not HEAD -- h src
```
   `--not HEAD` removes the PR's own commits (tron-4353: without it, `-S'TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT'` lists the PR's own 1dcb88ca28). Commits after the review date are not evidence. On 2287 the helper commit 45eb1fe682 (2026-03-27, Wado-posi) is an ancestor of BASE ba1bed266d, so step 2 at BASE already finds it; step 3 lists only this PR's own later merges (7eae660633, 99e5c61b1e).
4. Read both sides: `git -C WT show HEAD:<helper file> | sed -n '<a>,<b>p'` and the candidate's enclosing function. Write every difference: operand type and alignment (1920: the helper takes `volatile uint64_t*`, the V address at fcc9b0de95 hwattention.hpp:400/:405 is `- 6`, 2 bytes off 8-byte alignment); element state after the call (2461: `resize` fills `nullptr`, the loop fills `make_unique`); branches the owner has that the candidate lacks (2302: the softcapping branch reads `query_pre_attn_scalar`); the tokens twin branches differ by, from `diff <(git show HEAD:<file> | sed -n 'A1,A2p') <(git show HEAD:<file> | sed -n 'B1,B2p')` (2980: `weights_cmd_attn_fields` vs `weights_cmd_matmul_fields` and one space); statements between two adjacent loops (4258: none). When the candidate is a conjunction, match each conjunct: a conjunct the helper covers is replaced, one it does not cover stays (2287 at 1a88e897e1:827 keeps `have_devices &&`, replaces the getenv). A difference in the configuration knob itself (variable name, default, read-once) is not a do-not-fire reason.
5. For (g): confirm the added lines contain the whole sequence; then count copies at HEAD and which keep the comment, and date the sequence:
```
git -C WT grep -n -E 'reservation\.commit\(\)|guard\.commit\(\)|tracker(->|\.)push\(' HEAD -- h src
git -C WT grep -n 'Descriptors are live\|disarm rollback' HEAD -- h src
git -C WT log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -S'<call name>' -- <file>; gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/<sha>/pulls --jq '.[].number'
```
   On 4128: `-S'guard.commit()'` -> 576843b189 (2026-06-02, PR 2906, also the 'Descriptors are live' comment); `-S'reservation.commit()'` -> 2bae8c454b (2026-07-22, PR 3385). Wade wrote '#3928' in 3907214892; quote that as his attribution: the PR 3928 merge cb255d352d does not touch src/tron/gof.cpp.
6. For (a) across layers: `git -C WT show HEAD:README.code-org.md | sed -n '/Dependencies (aspirational)/,/^$/p'` ('Only tron/hardware should directly depend on pos/'). If the helper's header is in a layer the file must not include, the remedy is an `extern <signature>;` declaration (3016: Wade asked for it in device.cpp; the author put `namespace tron { extern bool fwd_hw_attn_enabled(); }` in h/libpos.hpp:29-31 (dca7ace69b), reached through h/pos/device.hpp:22, and src/pos/device.cpp:166 calls it at 39396c8728).
7. Report per candidate: new site file:line, owner file:line, the sites that already call the owner, the named difference (or 'none'), the smallest edit (call the helper; pass the stored member instead of the literal; one loop or `set_passes(passes, items)`; one dispatch helper for the copied sequence; never new infrastructure beyond the nearest helper). Add the step-1 counters: candidates per kind and drops per reason (2287: a=1 kept, b=0, c=1 dropped as comment line, d=0, e=0, f=5 dropped by body shape, g=8 dropped for no ordering comment, h=2 and i=4 dropped after reading the callee).

On PR 4596 (reviewed commit 0f784c44ff, BASE 66c7bb8db1): (a) one getenv added, `std::getenv("TRON_ATTN_STATS")` at h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:163; step 2 finds no other reader at HEAD or BASE, candidate cleared. (e) the diff adds `pool_worker` with body `return n_workers - n_attn_workers + attn_ix;` (attn_stats.hpp:431-435, prod.diff line 440); grep of the operands at HEAD h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp: inline `tp.num_workers() - n_attn_workers + worker_ix` at :797 (pre-existing at BASE :761, feeds `stats_ref.note_attn_job(pool_worker_ix, ...)` at :855 and the speedometer at :837), inline in a log string at :1498 (BASE :1396), helper calls at :1343 and :1485; named difference: none. Finding = Wade's 4147010638. At the commit he APPROVED, 441e81178b (2026-09-30T19:34Z), :856 calls `stats_ref.pool_worker(worker_ix, n_attn_workers)`, :797 stays for the speedometer at :837, and the log string at :1499 still spells the formula. (h)(i): 3 lines (attn_stats resize :386, :463; loop :1004), none a grow loop or a re-walked container.

On PR 2287 (reviewed commit 4274d5878a, BASE ba1bed266d, base hwattention_sync): (a) one hit, model.hpp:820 `if (have_devices && !getenv("TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN"))`; step 2 by stem HW_ATTN finds `fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` at hw_attn_config.hpp:17 with five callers at HEAD and at BASE; difference: the `have_devices` conjunct, kept at the fix 1a88e897e1:827. Finding = Wade's 3029194687.
final.widen_delta:
Adds a fourteenth check on production code. No existing check looks outside the diff for an implementation the new code repeats: check 4 is duplicate test coverage, check 13 is duplicate named constants, check 10 traces hunks to body claims. The new check reads h/ and src/ at HEAD and at BASE, the PR's base branch log before the review date, README.code-org.md for the layering rule, and the commit that introduced an ordered sequence. Boundaries stated in the do-not-fire list: a value a local or sibling member in the same scope already holds goes to the redundant-code check; a bare literal with no owner goes to check 13; a hot-path cost argument is a performance finding.

Words to add under "Words used here": helper (an existing function the project already calls for the same job); owner (the function or member that computes a value once); topic stem (an environment variable name with the TRON_/POS_ prefix and the USE_/DISABLE_ verb word stripped, e.g. HW_ATTN); layering rule (README.code-org.md "Dependencies (aspirational)": only tron/hardware may include pos/); mwaitx (the project's wait-until-a-memory-word-changes primitives, h/pos/mwaitx.hpp at early-2026 heads); getenv (a read of an environment variable).

The BASE definition in "Words used here" (`git merge-base HEAD origin/main`) must gain a clause: for a PR whose base branch is not main, BASE is the merge-base with that branch (`gh pr view N --json baseRefName`); check 14 depends on it (PR 2287 base hwattention_sync).

The description line of the skill gains "code that re-derives a value, predicate, wait or sequence an existing helper already provides". The "How Wade words a finding" section gains: he names the helper with its namespace and the sibling sites by line number, asks in question form for a primitive, and withdraws his own ask when the element type or alignment differs (3102275102).
